newsitem.title: USA: NYSE asked to review Chateau/ROC deal.
newsitem.headline: NYSE asked to review Chateau/ROC deal.

text.p: Oppenheimer and Co Inc said on Friday that it requested the New York Stock Exchange to review the merger deal between Chateau Properties Inc and ROC Communities Inc.

"We believe that actions that the companies have recently approved...may violate New York Stock Exchange listing requirements and cause the surviving company's stock to be delisted by the exchange," Oppenheimer said in a letter to the NYSE chairman Richard Grasso.
A copy of the letter was attached to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Oppenheimer which owns a stake of about seven percent in Chateau and less than five percent in ROC said the NYSE review should determine whether or not actions by the two companies will result in the delisting of the surviving company's stock.
Oppenheimer said it hoped that any NYSE decision would cause shareholders of the two companies to modify their actions "before the delisting becomes a fait accompli."
In seeking the review, Oppenheimer said the boards of Chateau and ROC did not respond to other offers made to acquire to Chateau.
Instead Chateau and ROC renegotiated their original merger deal in such a way as to completely nullify the effective voting power of shareholders, Oppenheimer said.

The renegotiated deal contains provisions designed to enable Chateau and ROC insiders and their managements to unilaterally "stuff the ballot" and ensure a favorable vote on the merger, Oppenheimer added.
